screenings.title: Out of the Blue
screenings.description: Co-written by Hou Hsiao-hsien and frequent collaborator Chu T’ien-wen, adapting her own short story, Chen’s minimalist coming-of-age drama centers on a crucial meeting between Jielong and Tangmi (Li Chih-Hsi and Li Chih-Chyi), high school sweethearts from very different class backgrounds who, three years after her abrupt disappearance, are reunited, so that Tangmi can inform the fiercely career-oriented Jielong that he’s in fact the father of her young child. Director of the previous year’s Golden Horse Award-winning Growing Up and cinematographer of Hou’s The Boys from Fengkuei, Chen would later say of Out of the Blue that it marked “the only time in my 60-year career that I made a film I truly wanted to make… approaching an unacceptable incident with calmness, tolerance and understanding.”

screenings.title: A Brighter Summer Day
screenings.description: A sprawling and intimate evocation of the Taiwan of Yang’s teenage years: the outset of the 1960s, a period defined by street gang activity, the political repression of the Kuomintang military government, and the ubiquity of American pop culture. A Brighter Summer Day takes its inspiration from the story of the country’s first juvenile homicide, with Chang Chen’s brooding outsider just one figure in Yang’s bustling tapestry, regarded in seemingly serene long takes that bristle with repressed emotion.

screenings.title: A Scanner Darkly | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: A Scanner Darkly screens as part of “2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die,” curated by Steve Macfarlane. Read the full series line-up HERE>>.

screenings.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
screenings.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage.

screenings.title: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: Maddie's Secret
screenings.description: Tuesday, June 16 at 7:00: Sneak Preview + Q&A with John Early Wednesday, June 17 at 7:00: Sneak Preview + Q&A with John Early and Carla Lalli Friday, June 19 at 2:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by John Wilson Friday, June 19 at 4:45: Q&A with John Early moderated by Brace Belden Friday, June 19 at 7:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Ivy Wolk Friday, June 10 at 9:45: Extended introduction by John Early Saturday, June 20 at 11:30: Q&A with John Early moderated by Julio Torres Saturday, June 20 at 2:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Theda Hammel Saturday, June 20 at 4:45: Q&A with John Early moderated by Sarah Sherman Saturday, June 20 at 7:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Amy Sedaris Saturday, June 20 at 9:45: Extended introduction by John Early

screenings.title: Union County
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: “A merciless, demoniac satire in the future imperfect. It posits a world somehow gone berserk, in which there are no real alternatives, only degrees of madness. Kubrick makes the whole thing (as he did in Dr. Strangelove) chillingly and often hilariously believable…. Malcolm McDowell is sensational. His performance has the range and dynamism that signal the arrival of a new superstar. As for Director Kubrick, his work is stylistically almost flawless. If there was any doubt after 2001, A Clockwork Orange confirms Kubrick as our most audacious film maker. There have been many visions of a malign future on film (1984, Things to Come, Fahrenheit 451) but none quite so unsparing and so ruthlessly witty.” – Jay Cocks, TIME

screenings.title: Stop Making Sense
screenings.description: Considered by critics as the greatest concert film of all time, STOP MAKING SENSE stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads’ most memorable songs.

screenings.title: anyone lived in a pretty how town
The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title:
You Had to Be There:
How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution…
screenings.description: “AN EXUBERANT AND ESSENTIAL DOC FOR COMEDY HEADS... The comedy revolution referred to by the title of Nick Davis’s sharp and effusive documentary YOU HAD TO BE THERE: HOW THE TORONTO GODSPELL IGNITED THE COMEDY REVOLUTION... is the one that took place on television in the ’70s: the creation of Saturday Night Live and SCTV and everything that grew out of them. YOU HAD TO BE THERE makes the case that the Petri dish from which the DNA of those shows was sprung was the 1972 Toronto production of Godspell, the Jesus-and-his-followers-as-hippie-clowns musical that had rocked the world when it premiered on Broadway the year before. The Toronto production featured a young Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Dave Thomas (all Canadian), and, from across the river, Detroit’s own Gilda Radner—who was the very first performer to be cast on Saturday Night, a show created by Lorne Michaels, who was also Canadian... There’s passionate testimony from the likes of Mike Myers and Lin-Manuel Miranda, who hails the show as ‘the ’27 Yankees of comedy.’ YOU HAD TO BE THERE shows you that something was in the air up there, and that it spread like the world’s happiest virus.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Director Nick Davis’ terrific return to this historic event offers a laugh-a-minute trip down memory lane that’s not merely nostalgic. It’s a valuable oral history of a defining moment in pop culture... A hugely entertaining record of Canadian cultural history worthy of time and celebration. And, in perhaps the most Canadian trait ever, it’s an American production.” – Pat Mullen, POV Magazine

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: On a String
screenings.description: Isabel (Isabel Hagen) is a young, Juilliard-trained violist still living at home with her parents in the heart of New York City. She’s trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends but when her toxic ex- boyfriend reappears, who also happens to be the Philharmonic’s “newest, hottest cellist,” he informs her of a viola opening in the prestigious orchestra. Nothing can go wrong, right?

screenings.title: My Brother's Wedding
screenings.description: “ONE OF AMERICA’S VERY BEST FILMMAKERS.” – Chicago Tribune “Burnett’s work is an indelible reminder of what real independence looks like. His early films in particular also testify to the vitality of a neorealist impulse that has never quite taken root in American cinema. KILLER OF SHEEP and MY BROTHER’S WEDDING have a sense of place and personality that is marvelous and rare.” – A.O. Scott, The New York Times “Shows us how deep (Burnett’s) humanist perspective goes, yielding more evidence of the subtlety and patience with which this filmmaker explores one of the great subjects of his career: the problem of dignity among a demoralized underclass.” – Andrew Chan, Slant

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: The Kingdom
screenings.description: On the pale, sun soaked island of Corsica in the summer of 1995, the teenage Lesia is plucked from her sheltered life, and taken to a remote villa where her fugitive mob boss father, Pierre-Paul, is hiding out. Pierre-Paul is a menacing figure, a near stranger to Lesia, and at first she feels trapped by the secrecy and danger which defines his life. But when an assassination attempt sets a chain of bloody vendettas in motion, Lesia and Pierre-Paul are forced to go on the run together. As they flee, Lesia becomes closer than ever with her father, and as they wade together through the violent underworld which he is entrenched in, his devotion to revenge begins to rub off on her. THE KINGDOM is a story of blood: blood spilled, blood sought, and the blood which binds us.

screenings.title: Who Moves America
screenings.description: In an era of deepening inequality, UPS Teamsters stand on the brink of a historic strike. As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Practical Magic 2
screenings.description: Practical Magic 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

screenings.title: Resident Evil (2026)
screenings.description: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. screenings.title: The Work in Progress

Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.description: She’s alive…yet dead! She’s dead…yet alive! Betsy Connell believed she had seen strange behavior from her patients, but nothing in her training and experience has prepared her for the voodoo, horror and walking undead of a Caribbean island in visionary director Jacques Tourneur’s I Walked with a Zombie. Pierre-Paul is a menacing figure, a near stranger to Lesia, and at first she feels trapped by the secrecy and danger which defines his life. screenings.title: Workingman's Death (w/intro)
screenings.description: A protege of fellow Austrian Ulrich Seidl, Glawogger was occasionally painted with the brush of “provocateur,” but his deep empathy, humor, and relentless curiosity guides his films even through the most challenging subject matter. His “Globalization Trilogy” is a triptych of documentaries loosely dealing with the effects of shifting economic markets and modernization on some of the world’s most disenfranchised workers — though Glawogger disliked the “Globalization” framing, eschewing academic detachment to emphasize his audience and subjects’ shared humanity. In each of these films, Glawogger avoids ethnographic trappings by placing his protagonists center stage, never trivializing or overtly romanticizing them even as they experience some of the harshest conditions imaginable.

Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... screenings.title:
You Had to Be There:
How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution…
screenings.description: “AN EXUBERANT AND ESSENTIAL DOC FOR COMEDY HEADS... The comedy revolution referred to by the title of Nick Davis’s sharp and effusive documentary YOU HAD TO BE THERE: HOW THE TORONTO GODSPELL IGNITED THE COMEDY REVOLUTION... is the one that took place on television in the ’70s: the creation of Saturday Night Live and SCTV and everything that grew out of them. YOU HAD TO BE THERE makes the case that the Petri dish from which the DNA of those shows was sprung was the 1972 Toronto production of Godspell, the Jesus-and-his-followers-as-hippie-clowns musical that had rocked the world when it premiered on Broadway the year before. The Toronto production featured a young Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Dave Thomas (all Canadian), and, from across the river, Detroit’s own Gilda Radner—who was the very first performer to be cast on Saturday Night, a show created by Lorne Michaels, who was also Canadian... There’s passionate testimony from the likes of Mike Myers and Lin-Manuel Miranda, who hails the show as ‘the ’27 Yankees of comedy.’ YOU HAD TO BE THERE shows you that something was in the air up there, and that it spread like the world’s happiest virus.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Director Nick Davis’ terrific return to this historic event offers a laugh-a-minute trip down memory lane that’s not merely nostalgic. It’s a valuable oral history of a defining moment in pop culture... A hugely entertaining record of Canadian cultural history worthy of time and celebration. And, in perhaps the most Canadian trait ever, it’s an American production.” – Pat Mullen, POV Magazine

Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Union County
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

Brash, abusive junkyard owner Harry (Paul Leder, giving a manic performance that must be seen to be believed) quickly tries to implicate Ben in his shady dealings, while Harry’s beautiful but broken kept woman Poochie (McClanahan) tries her best to shake the foundations of his middle-class morality. Meanwhile, Edna finds herself pursued by Harry’s disturbed employee Blowhard (King Moody), while tortured poet/car thief Floyd (Norman Hartweg) muses on Freud and Nietzsche.

screenings.title: The Vanishing Song

As residents, conservationists, and wildlife authorities unite to translocate him to a national park, one question remains: leave him, move him, or risk losing him altogether? Inspired by the late Dr. Jane Goodall, The Vanishing Song follows the race to get him home.

As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Evita
screenings.description: Don’t cry for her, Argentina—after years of dauntless campaigning, Madonna landed the coveted role of actress-cum-First Lady Eva Perón in this lavish, costume-change-a-minute adaptation of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber’s 1978 stage musical, featuring Jonathan Pryce as the statesman who shares his power and his bed with Eva, and Antonio Banderas as narrator of her meteoric rise and tragic end. “Evita is actually a very visual movie, and Alan Parker is probably one of the most exciting and visual directors I have ever worked with… He wanted to make the film look very real, almost like a newsreel, but also very glamorous at the same time… There were certain scenes where we had up to 4,000 or 5,000 extras, because Alan didn’t want to use any special effects—he wanted it all to be in front of the lens.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: The Kingdom
screenings.description: On the pale, sun soaked island of Corsica in the summer of 1995, the teenage Lesia is plucked from her sheltered life, and taken to a remote villa where her fugitive mob boss father, Pierre-Paul, is hiding out. Pierre-Paul is a menacing figure, a near stranger to Lesia, and at first she feels trapped by the secrecy and danger which defines his life. But when an assassination attempt sets a chain of bloody vendettas in motion, Lesia and Pierre-Paul are forced to go on the run together. As they flee, Lesia becomes closer than ever with her father, and as they wade together through the violent underworld which he is entrenched in, his devotion to revenge begins to rub off on her. THE KINGDOM is a story of blood: blood spilled, blood sought, and the blood which binds us.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 2: the Unrecovered
screenings.description: The attacks were encoded in the national memory over seemingly endless minutes, hours, days, weeks, and months of media coverage. A quarter of a century later, it is tempting to think of 9/11 as a media event announcing material reality’s final, total subordination to the image—as Baudrillard said, “They did it. We wished it.” Yet to conceive of 9/11 in only these terms would be to overlook the lived horrors of the day and the insidious reverberations of a nationwide psychic trauma. From our historical vantage, the events of September 11 seem as fundamental to our current reality as the air we breathe. In recognition of the twenty-fifth anniversary of September 11, 2001, Spectacle presents a selection of films that confront the phenomenal and psychic impact of the attacks, and the indelible scar they left on the world. There was before, and this is after. Program 1: REICHSTAG 9/11 & DISINTEGRATION LOOP 1.1 REICHSTAG 9/11 Dir. Ken Jacobs, 2016. United States. 38 min. Silent.

screenings.description: Dir. Robert Berry. 1963, 71 mins. U.S. DCP. With Robert Berry, Pauline Elliott. A frustrated author is plagued by recurring nightmares centered around a haunted house in House of Dreams, where the boundaries of reality do not blur because they never existed in the first place. Shot on gritty 16mm film stock in Indiana and never legitimately distributed, House of Dreams is a hidden chapter of mid-century, avant garde horror from director/star Robert Berry that is as haunting as it is sincere. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Climate Film Festival Opening Night: House of Fish
screenings.description: Followed by a discussion with director Santiago Burin des Roziers and reception House of Fish Dir. Santiago Burin des Roziers. 2026, 85 mins. In Italian with English subtitles. At the crossroads of art, activism, and the ocean lies the extraordinary story of Paolo Fanciulli, a humble Italian fisherman with a revolutionary vision. After witnessing decades of destruction caused by illegal bottom trawling, Paolo devised a bold solution: an underwater museum of monumental marble sculptures that protect the seabed by preventing trawling while standing as powerful symbols of hope and resistance. House of Fish follows his remarkable journey, blending intimate personal storytelling with a natural history perspective on the fragile Mediterranean ecosystem. Through breathtaking underwater cinematography, the film reveals the devastating impact of industrial fishing on endangered marine life and vital habitats, including Posidonia oceanica, a seagrass essential to biodiversity and carbon capture. More than a conservation documentary, House of Fish is a cinematic celebration of courage, creativity, and community, inspiring audiences to reconnect with the ocean and recognize that one person’s vision can help transform the future of our seas. East Coast premiere. Followed by a reception from 9:00-11:00 p.m. Tickets: $20 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order Tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. About the Climate Film Festival: The Climate Film Festival (CFF) is both an annual film festival held in New York City during Climate Week NYC and a year-round nonprofit cultural organization. Founded in 2023, CFF harnesses the power of motion pictures to reshape the conversation around climate change, making urgent issues accessible, engaging, and action-oriented through the cinematic lens. Each year, the festival presents a curated selection of scripted, documentary, feature, short, episodic, and experimental works, alongside filmmaker conversations, educational programming, and the Narrative Change Summit. Committed to formal innovation, environmental justice, and community engagement, CFF amplifies bold voices and inspiring films that reframe the conversation around climate action. Special Guest: Santiago Burin des Roziers was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina and moved to London to pursue a career in filmmaking. Not long after film school, he started directing. His projects have taken him around the globe, to over 30 countries. He has made films for the BBC, Channel 4 and VICE, as well as for brands such as Coca– Cola, Sony, Red Bull, and Adidas.

screenings.title: The Blade
screenings.description: Tsui’s masterful tribute to the martial arts films he grew up with, paying homage in particular to Chang Cheh’s 1967 wuxia landmark The One-Armed Swordsman, The Blade tells the tale of a blacksmith (Vincent Zhao) at a foundry specializing in sword manufacture who, on learning the identity of his father’s killer—tatted-up bad man Hung Yan-yan—sets out to see justice done. A dervish-like work of phantasmagoric action filmmaking that boasts rapid cutting, berserk camera movement, insanely intricate choreography, smothering closer-than-close-ups, and compositions splashed with theatrical gels. Tsui has never been anyone’s idea of a minimalist, but The Blade is what you get when he’s really firing on all cylinders: euphoric sensory overload.

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: The Witch Hunt
screenings.description: Set in the mountains of rugged western Norway in the early years of the 17th century, The Witch Hunt reunites Breien with Games of Love and Loneliness star Lil Terselius, here playing Eli—a young woman who returns to her native village after the failure of her marriage to find the locals in the grips of a superstitious persecutorial mania, a certitude that witches dwell in their midst, and a determination, on the part of the local patriarchs, to bring their punitive powers to bear against women who don’t tow the line. A film of somber beauty, winner of a Special Mention for Historical Reconstruction and a Best Actress prize at the 1981 Venice Film Festival.

screenings.title: The Kingdom
screenings.description: On the pale, sun soaked island of Corsica in the summer of 1995, the teenage Lesia is plucked from her sheltered life, and taken to a remote villa where her fugitive mob boss father, Pierre-Paul, is hiding out. Pierre-Paul is a menacing figure, a near stranger to Lesia, and at first she feels trapped by the secrecy and danger which defines his life. But when an assassination attempt sets a chain of bloody vendettas in motion, Lesia and Pierre-Paul are forced to go on the run together. As they flee, Lesia becomes closer than ever with her father, and as they wade together through the violent underworld which he is entrenched in, his devotion to revenge begins to rub off on her. THE KINGDOM is a story of blood: blood spilled, blood sought, and the blood which binds us.

screenings.title: Bad Apples
screenings.description: A primary school teacher accidentally locks her most disruptive student in her home. Desperate to undo it, she hesitates when her class begins to flourish in the child’s absence, landing her in an impossible predicament.

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

screenings.title: The Fisherman
screenings.description: A traditional Ghanaian fisherman forced into retirement teams up with a bougie talking fish and his quirky associates on a whimsical adventure to Accra – chasing the dream of owning a boat while learning to navigate the modern world without losing touch with their roots.

screenings.title: Resident Evil (2026)
screenings.description: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Who's Watching + Q&A
screenings.description: Caleb, an awkward and obsessive office worker and aspiring filmmaker, fixates on his new manager, Krista. Claiming to be making a documentary, he records every moment of his life and the people around him—often without consent. As his delusions deepen, Caleb’s harmless-seeming awkwardness warps into invasive surveillance, stalking, and escalating violations of Krista’s privacy. His troubled past, unstable home life, and growing resentment fuel a disturbing descent that endangers everyone around him as reality and his self-made “film” begin to blur.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Practical Magic 2
screenings.description: Practical Magic 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

screenings.title: Motorama
screenings.description: Gus (Jordan Christopher Michael), a ten year old runaway obsessed with winning $500 million dollars from the collect-‘em-all roadside card game MOTORAMA, cashes in his piggy bank and steals his deadbeat dad’s cherry red Mustang. He bops from gas station to gas station across a cynical, surrealist landscape of rotting Americana, encountering a series of increasingly deranged, violent characters on his way to the Chimera Gas Company’s corporate headquarters to learn the truth about the prize at the end of the highway.

screenings.title: Knock Off
screenings.description: Tsui’s second and last English-language film, reuniting him with the star of his 1997 Double Team and favorite of Hong Kongers making forays into Hollywood, Jean-Claude Van Damme. In Hong Kong arranging a fashion show for “V-Six” jeans, unscrupulous designer JCVD and partner Rob Schneider discover their product has been swapped with cheap fakes, and follow the trail of counterfeit denim into intrigues involving the Russian mob, a CIA base inside a Buddha statue, exploding nanobombs hidden in jean studs, and a lot of thunderous roundhouse kicks. While Tsui embraces the silliness of the setup, he’s a serious filmmaker working with consistent thematic motifs, here creating a world of false fronts where nothing is as it seems.

screenings.title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
screenings.description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: “A merciless, demoniac satire in the future imperfect. It posits a world somehow gone berserk, in which there are no real alternatives, only degrees of madness. Kubrick makes the whole thing (as he did in Dr. Strangelove) chillingly and often hilariously believable…. Malcolm McDowell is sensational. His performance has the range and dynamism that signal the arrival of a new superstar. As for Director Kubrick, his work is stylistically almost flawless. If there was any doubt after 2001, A Clockwork Orange confirms Kubrick as our most audacious film maker. There have been many visions of a malign future on film (1984, Things to Come, Fahrenheit 451) but none quite so unsparing and so ruthlessly witty.” – Jay Cocks, TIME

screenings.title: Angel's Egg
screenings.description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two.

screenings.title: Resident Evil (2026)

screenings.title: Popstar: Never Stop Never Stopping
screenings.description: “POPSTAR: NEVER STOP NEVER STOPPING is a 2016 mockumentary by The Lonely Island. The movie follows the life of popstar Connor4Real as he releases his second solo album. The film flopped at the box office, making back under half of its budget, but has since gained a cult following.

screenings.title: Stop Making Sense
screenings.description: Considered by critics as the greatest concert film of all time, STOP MAKING SENSE stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads’ most memorable songs.

screenings.title: The Hang-up
screenings.description: From this familiar premise – the innocents unknowingly walking into a den of vice – Hayes crafts a powerful chamber piece that plays like Tennessee Williams dragged into a (literal) trash heap. Brash, abusive junkyard owner Harry (Paul Leder, giving a manic performance that must be seen to be believed) quickly tries to implicate Ben in his shady dealings, while Harry’s beautiful but broken kept woman Poochie (McClanahan) tries her best to shake the foundations of his middle-class morality. Meanwhile, Edna finds herself pursued by Harry’s disturbed employee Blowhard (King Moody), while tortured poet/car thief Floyd (Norman Hartweg) muses on Freud and Nietzsche.

screenings.title: Mac and Me
screenings.description: A wheelchair-bound boy helps to reunite an earthbound alien with its extraterrestrial family in this shameless rip-off of Steven Spielberg’s E.T.. Separated from his parents shortly after arriving on planet Earth, a Mysterious Alien Creature (MAC) quickly strikes up a friendship with lonely Eric Cruise (former Easter Seals spokesman Jade Calegory). New to town and in need of a pal after losing his father, Eric discovers just how amazing the universe can be when mischievous MAC takes him on the adventure of a lifetime.

screenings.title: The Vanishing Song
screenings.description: Han is a wild lar gibbon living where he shouldn’t be — trapped between highways and housing estates in a Malaysian city, swinging through power lines, his haunting calls answered by no one. As residents, conservationists, and wildlife authorities unite to translocate him to a national park, one question remains: leave him, move him, or risk losing him altogether? Inspired by the late Dr. Jane Goodall, The Vanishing Song follows the race to get him home.

screenings.title: Who Moves America
screenings.description: In an era of deepening inequality, UPS Teamsters stand on the brink of a historic strike. As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: Peggy Sue Got Married
screenings.description: Peggy Sue Bodell is a pretty, buoyant mother of two recently separated from her husband. Attending her 25th high school reunion alone, she faints and wakes up to find herself once again a senior in high school in 1959. Although she appears to her classmates as a 17-year-old bobby-soxer, Peggy Sue has her adult memory and perspective, from which she is able to enjoy the delicious, if at times heartbreaking, ability to revisit the past while knowing what the future holds. Able to take chances she never took, Peggy Sue does her best to right a few wrongs, but it’s the insight she gains into her relationship with her husband-to-be that may actually do her some good-once she gets back to the present.

screenings.title: Arsa
screenings.description: Arsa is aged eighteen or so. She is beautiful, introverted and wild. She lives alone in a rundown hovel overlooking the sea, somewhere on the edge of an island. One day, three youngsters arrive on the island and rent a holiday home. All of a sudden, Arsa’s world is invaded. Andrea, one of the boys, captivated by Arsa’s enigmatic presence, tries to migrate into her world and discovers her shocking desire…

screenings.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
screenings.description: More than 30 years after Iran’s Ayatollah Khomeini called for the death of author Salman Rushdie over the publication of The Satanic Verses, Rushdie traveled to Chautauqua, NY to speak about the US as a sanctuary for exiled artists. At his talk, a young man rushed the stage, intent on killing him with a knife. Using Rushdie’s works, including his powerful memoir Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder, Oscar winning documentarian Gibney crafts a striking testament to freedom of expression and a defiant response to the attempt on Rushdie’s life.

screenings.title: Paprika
screenings.description: The fourth and final film by Kon takes place in a not-too-distant future in which therapists, using a new technology called DC Mini, are able to record the dreams of psychiatric patients. All well and good, until a raid on the lab leads to the loss of the DC Mini prototype and a bleed between the troubled subconscious images and reality, leading to a race-against-time to stop bedlam from breaking out in the streets. An admitted inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s Inception (2010), though far more visually extravagant in its vibrant, psychedelia-inflected imaginings, which climax in a thrilling, terrifying dream apocalypse burst from Kon’s fervid imagination.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Your Name. (10th Anniversary)
screenings.description: Dir. Makoto Shinkai. 2016, 106 mins. DCP. In Japanese with English subtitles. MoMI brings Shinkai’s 2016 beloved animated fantasy Your Name. back to the big screen on the occasion of its tenth anniversary. On the eve of a rare cosmic event—the passing of a once-in-a-lifetime comet—two high school students, strangers living separate lives, suddenly switch places. Mitsuha wakes up in Taki’s body and he, hers. Communicating through scribbled notes and phone diaries, they muddle through each other’s lives in both frustrating and hilarious ways. What opens as a teen romance expands into a mystery touching upon Shinto rites and the supernatural. Your Name. captures the longing for lost places and people, underscored by Shinkai’s gorgeous hyper-realist style indelibly etching Tokyo’s cityscape and the beauty of rural Gifu prefecture—and the ubiquitous trains threading through them—into the viewer’s memory. Featuring music by the Japanese band RADWIMPS. View trailer. Recommended for ages 9+ Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Purchase tickets for September 19 at 12:00 p.m. (Redstone theater) Purchase tickets for September 20 at 2:00 p.m. (Bartos theater) Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Oedipus Rex
screenings.description: Seeking source materials from which to forge a new “primal cinema,” Pasolini delved into the storehouse of mythic heritage. Taking on Sophocles’s Oedipus Rex, he begins with a prologue set in prewar Italy, and goes on to defy expectation throughout, depicting Oedipus (Franco Citti), unknowingly betrothed to biological mother Silvana Mangano, as a victim of his own ignorant innocence, here far from an unambiguously positive virtue. Pasolini’s first film in color, featuring costumes and art direction that evoke an almost science fiction vision of the ancient world, and a showy role for Carmelo Bene, then-reigning bad boy of Italian stage and screen.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: 2026 Sundance Festival Short Film Tour (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: My Brother's Wedding
screenings.description: “ONE OF AMERICA’S VERY BEST FILMMAKERS.” – Chicago Tribune “Burnett’s work is an indelible reminder of what real independence looks like. His early films in particular also testify to the vitality of a neorealist impulse that has never quite taken root in American cinema. KILLER OF SHEEP and MY BROTHER’S WEDDING have a sense of place and personality that is marvelous and rare.” – A.O. Scott, The New York Times “Shows us how deep (Burnett’s) humanist perspective goes, yielding more evidence of the subtlety and patience with which this filmmaker explores one of the great subjects of his career: the problem of dignity among a demoralized underclass.” – Andrew Chan, Slant

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: My Brother's Wedding
screenings.description: “ONE OF AMERICA’S VERY BEST FILMMAKERS.” – Chicago Tribune “Burnett’s work is an indelible reminder of what real independence looks like. His early films in particular also testify to the vitality of a neorealist impulse that has never quite taken root in American cinema. KILLER OF SHEEP and MY BROTHER’S WEDDING have a sense of place and personality that is marvelous and rare.” – A.O. Scott, The New York Times “Shows us how deep (Burnett’s) humanist perspective goes, yielding more evidence of the subtlety and patience with which this filmmaker explores one of the great subjects of his career: the problem of dignity among a demoralized underclass.” – Andrew Chan, Slant

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Notes Toward an African Orestes
screenings.description: Pasolini’s thrillingly freeform, intellectually adventurous documentary, narrated in the style of thoughts dashed off in a notebook, charts his preparations to make a film of Aeschylus’s Oresteia trilogy in Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Uganda. Forming a trilogy of sorts with previous Greek tragedy adaptations Oedipus Rex and Medea—a trilogy that, in the phrasing of scholar Daniel Humphrey, encapsulates Pasolini’s paradoxical “archaic modernism”—Notes Toward an African Orestes proposes metaphorical parallels between the source texts and events following the emergence of many African nations into independence, and also finds the filmmaker testing his own presumptions and prejudices against the lived experience of African students at the University of Rome.

screenings.title: Bad Apples
screenings.description: A primary school teacher accidentally locks her most disruptive student in her home. Desperate to undo it, she hesitates when her class begins to flourish in the child’s absence, landing her in an impossible predicament.

screenings.title:
You Had to Be There:
How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution…
screenings.description: “AN EXUBERANT AND ESSENTIAL DOC FOR COMEDY HEADS... The comedy revolution referred to by the title of Nick Davis’s sharp and effusive documentary YOU HAD TO BE THERE: HOW THE TORONTO GODSPELL IGNITED THE COMEDY REVOLUTION... is the one that took place on television in the ’70s: the creation of Saturday Night Live and SCTV and everything that grew out of them. YOU HAD TO BE THERE makes the case that the Petri dish from which the DNA of those shows was sprung was the 1972 Toronto production of Godspell, the Jesus-and-his-followers-as-hippie-clowns musical that had rocked the world when it premiered on Broadway the year before. The Toronto production featured a young Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Dave Thomas (all Canadian), and, from across the river, Detroit’s own Gilda Radner—who was the very first performer to be cast on Saturday Night, a show created by Lorne Michaels, who was also Canadian... There’s passionate testimony from the likes of Mike Myers and Lin-Manuel Miranda, who hails the show as ‘the ’27 Yankees of comedy.’ YOU HAD TO BE THERE shows you that something was in the air up there, and that it spread like the world’s happiest virus.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Director Nick Davis’ terrific return to this historic event offers a laugh-a-minute trip down memory lane that’s not merely nostalgic. It’s a valuable oral history of a defining moment in pop culture... A hugely entertaining record of Canadian cultural history worthy of time and celebration. And, in perhaps the most Canadian trait ever, it’s an American production.” – Pat Mullen, POV Magazine

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: Wild Inside
screenings.description: Screening followed by a Q&A with producer Gabriel Sedgwick, film participant Suzanne Highland of Wild Bird Fund and Novem Auyeung, PhD, Director of Research & Monitoring, Environment & Planning for NYC Parks Dir. Penny Lane. 2026, 95 mins. U.S. DCP. Flaco, a Eurasian Eagle-Owl, escapes from the Central Park Zoo and sets off on a magical odyssey through the island of Manhattan. An apex predator with 2-inch talons, a 6-foot wingspan and piercing pumpkin-orange eyes, Flaco overcomes his years of captivity and lack of survival skills to answer the call of the wild—and discovers he was wild inside all along. This one-of-a-kind owl’s epic song is sung in Wild Inside by a chorus of besotted New Yorkers—young and old, bird-nerds and civilians, many of them immigrants themselves—all of them reaching for a glimpse of the wild, a glimmer of magic, or even just someone to believe in. The remarkable story of Flaco raises some questions: is it right to keep a bird in a cage? How can we be better to our nonhuman neighbors? Courtesy Sandbox Films. Watch the trailer here. Free with RSVP. Seating is first come, first served. Open Worlds: Science is funded by Simons Foundation International and administered by the Simons Foundation’s Science, Society & Culture division.

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Hell’s Highway: The True Story of Highway Safety Films | Sex, Death, Cars!
screenings.description: Critically-acclaimed upon it’s 2003 theatrical release, Hell’s Highway: The True Story of Highway Safety Films is a morbidly curious exploration of the shocking driver education films of yesteryear. Produced between 1959 and 1979 in Mansfield, Ohio, films such as Signal 30 encouraged safety by force-feeding high school kids color footage of careless driving’s dark consequences: blood-stained wreckage, injured bodies, fresh corpses. In the 1970s and ‘80s, these traumatic films disappeared from the American classroom and assumed an almost mythical status. Hell’s Highway unearths these artifacts of grim Americana and interviews the filmmakers responsible for this radical educational movement. This remastered edition includes three complete “blood-on-the-highway” films, newly restored from the original 16mm camera elements preserved in the Richard Prelinger Collection at the Library of Congress..

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
screenings.description: More than 30 years after Iran’s Ayatollah Khomeini called for the death of author Salman Rushdie over the publication of The Satanic Verses, Rushdie traveled to Chautauqua, NY to speak about the US as a sanctuary for exiled artists. At his talk, a young man rushed the stage, intent on killing him with a knife. Using Rushdie’s works, including his powerful memoir Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder, Oscar winning documentarian Gibney crafts a striking testament to freedom of expression and a defiant response to the attempt on Rushdie’s life.

screenings.title: Games of Love and Loneliness
screenings.description: Adapted from the novel A Serious Game by Swedish author Hjalmar Söderberg, whose play Gertrud had been the source for Carl Theodor Dreyer’s final film of the same title, Games of Love and Loneliness stars Stefan Ekman as Arvid, a young newspaperman who prioritizes professional ambitions over personal considerations so much as to pause his passionate romance with Lydia (Lil Terselius) just shy of wedding vows—complicating matters when the death of her father leaves Lydia in precarious circumstances and open to the prospect of a marriage of convenience. A handsomely mounted and deeply felt period melodrama spanning the years between 1897 and 1912, redolent with regret concerning opportunities not seized and roads not taken.

screenings.title: Resident Evil (2026)
screenings.description: From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

screenings.title: Checkout
screenings.description: This psychedelic dark comedy follows Dov, a desperate Jewish-American spy, who must convince his Israeli peers he is telling the truth about a legendary terrorist. A thirst to belong consumes his soul as he is forced to retell and remodel his adventure, all the while creating an intelligence fiasco.

screenings.title: The Kingdom
screenings.description: On the pale, sun soaked island of Corsica in the summer of 1995, the teenage Lesia is plucked from her sheltered life, and taken to a remote villa where her fugitive mob boss father, Pierre-Paul, is hiding out. Pierre-Paul is a menacing figure, a near stranger to Lesia, and at first she feels trapped by the secrecy and danger which defines his life. But when an assassination attempt sets a chain of bloody vendettas in motion, Lesia and Pierre-Paul are forced to go on the run together. As they flee, Lesia becomes closer than ever with her father, and as they wade together through the violent underworld which he is entrenched in, his devotion to revenge begins to rub off on her. THE KINGDOM is a story of blood: blood spilled, blood sought, and the blood which binds us.

screenings.title: Practical Magic 2
screenings.description: Practical Magic 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Viva Las Vegas + Learning from Learning from Las Vegas
screenings.description: All musically gifted race-driver Lucky Jackson (Elvis Presley) wants in Las Vegas is to score enough money for a new car motor so he can win the Grand Prix. When he encounters sexy swimming instructor Rusty (Ann-Margret), he considers staying around longer. After Lucky loses his winnings in the hotel pool, he’s forced to remain in Vegas long enough to win back his dough — but now he also wants to win Rusty’s heart. Unfortunately, so does his slick racing enemy, Elmo (Cesare Danova).
screenings.country: Learning from Learning from Las Vegas Musical, Comedy

screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 3: Circling Zero
screenings.description: The attacks were encoded in the national memory over seemingly endless minutes, hours, days, weeks, and months of media coverage. A quarter of a century later, it is tempting to think of 9/11 as a media event announcing material reality’s final, total subordination to the image—as Baudrillard said, “They did it. We wished it.” Yet to conceive of 9/11 in only these terms would be to overlook the lived horrors of the day and the insidious reverberations of a nationwide psychic trauma. From our historical vantage, the events of September 11 seem as fundamental to our current reality as the air we breathe. In recognition of the twenty-fifth anniversary of September 11, 2001, Spectacle presents a selection of films that confront the phenomenal and psychic impact of the attacks, and the indelible scar they left on the world. There was before, and this is after. Program 1: REICHSTAG 9/11 & DISINTEGRATION LOOP 1.1 REICHSTAG 9/11 Dir. Ken Jacobs, 2016. United States. 38 min. Silent.

screenings.title: Who Moves America (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: In an era of deepening inequality, UPS Teamsters stand on the brink of a historic strike. As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: Next of Kin
screenings.description: Childless and unmarried, wealthy shipping magnate Kai Skaug has keeled over at age 54. With great expectations, his extended family—elderly mother, brother and sister with attendant spouses and offspring, assorted cousins—gather for his funeral and the reading of his will… thence to discover that this motley group, many very nearly strangers to one another, have been condemned to close collaboration, only to receive their share of inheritance if they agree to jointly operate the business that the late tycoon built as equal partners. An ensemble cast battle royale in which old resentments resurface alongside deep-buried secrets and bouts of blood-on-the-balls bickering alternate with episodes of remorseful self-recrimination, premiered in the main competition at the 32nd Cannes Film Festival.

screenings.title: Arsa
screenings.description: Arsa is aged eighteen or so. She is beautiful, introverted and wild. She lives alone in a rundown hovel overlooking the sea, somewhere on the edge of an island. One day, three youngsters arrive on the island and rent a holiday home. All of a sudden, Arsa’s world is invaded. Andrea, one of the boys, captivated by Arsa’s enigmatic presence, tries to migrate into her world and discovers her shocking desire…

screenings.title: Titane | Sex, Death, Cars!
screenings.description: With a titanium plate surgically fused to her skull following a car crash as a child, car model Alexia embarks on a wild and ultimately unpredictable journey that questions our assumptions about family, identity and love. Winner of the Palm d’Or at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival.

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

Notorious for his sharp wit, the openly gay Bernal was a subversive ironist and a committed feminist. His films frequently used the roles of women to skewer what he saw as a sick society under the Marcos regime, best summed up by a line from his provocatively-titled essay Why The Martial Law Will Affect Your Sex Life: “Here we are, being practically ruled by a stranger who shall parade the chills and fevers of his ego and what are we going to do about it? We are going to be gripped by hysteria, that’s what.” This attitude culminated in the consensus pick for his masterpiece, Himala (1982), a study of the blind faith of the Philippines and the grip of hysteria that comes with it – it has only been vindicated with the country’s election of another Ferdinand Marcos to the Presidency. Bernal has subsequently remained a touchstone for the two key figures from the subsequent Third Golden Age: Spectacle favorites Lav Diaz and Raya Martin.

KILLER OF SHEEP and MY BROTHER’S WEDDING have a sense of place and personality that is marvelous and rare.” – A.O. Scott, The New York Times “Shows us how deep (Burnett’s) humanist perspective goes, yielding more evidence of the subtlety and patience with which this filmmaker explores one of the great subjects of his career: the problem of dignity among a demoralized underclass.” – Andrew Chan, Slant
